To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The use of a CNN pre-trained on ImageNet for object detection in the RGB-D domain is beneficial.

(1) deep convolutional networks trained on ImageNet perform well in the domain of RGBD object recognition in bin picking and (2) the DenseCap captioning model can be used to detect objects and segment them into parts in cluttered scenes.

(1) the use of pretrained models is a powerful tool to reduce the need for annotated data, (2) the combination of RGB and depth images can provide a good basis for the perception of cluttered bin picking tasks, and (3) the use of semantic segmentation is beneficial for object recognition in cluttered environments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the use of pretrained models is a promising approach for data-efficient deep learning for robotic applications.
our system was the first to make use of a full CNN based semantic segmentation pipeline for object detection and the first to use the DenseCap pipeline for object detection.
our team NimbRo was able to place 2nd and 3rd in both the pick and stow tasks of the Amazon Picking Competition 2016.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning models can be successfully applied to real world robotic problems with very little domain specific training data, as long as the models can be transferred from related tasks.
it is possible to achieve state-of-the-art performance in a real-world robotic application with a small amount of training data.
it is possible to build a competitive vision system for bin picking with only 1000 images and a few hours of annotation time.
